newsitem.title: USA: U.S. aims to reveal Elk Hills field buyers in Oct..
newsitem.headline: U.S. aims to reveal Elk Hills field buyers in Oct..

text.p: The U.S. Energy Department expects to be able to announce the winning bidders for its stake in the Elk Hills oil and gas field in October, assistant energy secretary Patricia Fry Godley said Wednesday.
Offers for the government's roughly 78 percent stake in the field, put up for sale Wednesday, are due October 1.

Choosing the winner or winners should "not take more than three or four weeks at the most," depending on how many offers there are and how the government decides to combine the offers to maximize the sale price, Godley said at a news briefing.
"My guess is it would be within a two-to-three week period," she added.
By law, the government is required to close the sale by February 10, 1998, as long as the offers it receives meet or exceed a minimum sales price, which the department plans to set this fall.
In an agreement reached this week with the co-owner of the field, Chevron Corp's Chevron USA Inc, the government settled the exact share it would offer in each of the field's four producing zones.

Chevron agreed that the government could put up for sale a 79.6 percent share in the Stevens Zone, 83.9 percent in the Dry Gas Zone, 70.0 percent in the Shallow Oil Zone, and 100 percent in the Carneros Zone.

However, the company and the Energy Department have yet to settle their equity shares for past production, which will be worked out in an agreement separate from the government's sale and will not involve the winning buyer or buyers.
The Energy Department said it was offering its stake in two types of interests.

One operating interest would give the buyer at least a 51 percent stake in each of the four producing zones, and the rest would be offered in several non-operating interests, each worth the equivalent of two percent of the government's stake.
